title: Our Team
text:
Professor of Forest Management Email | ResearchGate
Welcome! I am an Assistant Professor at the École de foresterie, Université de Moncton (Edmundston). My research focuses on understanding how climate change is reshaping forests, with an emphasis on landscape-level forest management, spatial analytics, and data-driven modeling. I develop and apply tools to quantify climate impacts and support adaptive management strategies for resilient forest ecosystems across North America.

title: Climate Change and Forest Ecosystems Lab
text:
Welcome to the Climate Change and Forest Ecosystems Lab. We are based at the École de Foresterie de l’Université de Moncton Campus d’Edmundston, where we bridge the gap between forest ecology and computational analytics.
Our mission is to quantify climate change impacts on forest ecosystems and develop adaptive management strategies that support the long-term sustainability of forest biomes across North America.

title: Partners
text:
The NHRI is a primary partner in our efforts to develop adaptive silviculture tools. With NHRI, we investigate the potential decline of deciduous tree species in the Acadian forest of New Brunswick under climate change and work toward solutions for the forest industry.
Visit Website





  



Ouranos is a key research partner that provides high-quality future climate data derived from a range of widely accepted climate models, supporting our work in climate change impact assessment and adaptation planning.

title: Partners

University Partners


  


Université Laval - Faculté de foresterie, de géographie et de géomatique
In collaboration with Dr. Loïc D’Orangeville, we conduct research on tree species migration and seedling performance under climate change. We also collaborate with Dr. Guillaume Moreau on maple syrup production, silviculture, and ecology under climate change.
Visit Website





  


University of New Brunswick - Forestry & Environmental Management
In collaboration with Dr. Anthony Taylor, we conduct research on the adaptation of landscape-level forest planning to climate change.

title: Join the Lab
text:
If you are interested in forest management, climate change adaptation, or spatial analytics, we would love to hear from you.


Assistant Professor Email: cedric.albert@umoncton.ca





We are always looking for motivated students to join the École de foresterie at the Edmundston campus. The Université de Moncton is a French-language university; therefore, candidates are expected to have functional proficiency in French for presentations, reports, exams, and interactions with other students. However, research activities and publications may be conducted in English, according to the candidate’s preference.


Our undergraduate program provides a strong foundation in forest ecology, geomatics, and sustainable management.
Learn More



We offer thesis-based Master’s projects focusing on climate change impacts and adaptive silviculture. Students benefit from close proximity to the Acadian forest and strong ties with industrial partners.
Learn More





Research is often a multi-institutional effort. We co-supervise PhD students registered at our partner institutions. You can still reach out to Dr. Albert to arrange a project and a supervision team.






PhD in Forestry



Prospective PhD students can pursue doctoral research under the co-supervision of Dr. Albert while registered any other Universities. We already have collaborators at:

Université Laval (FFGG)
University of New Brunswick (ForEM)













Application Instructions



If you are interested in a position, please email Dr. Albert with the following:

A brief statement of interest
Your CV.
A copy of your unofficial transcripts.
